evidence:
Source review, not a configured-judge result. I inspected the actual frozen XLSX with openpyxl: Quality Checks!A34:D34 is row 33, criterion_description_is_self_consistent, requiring ONE full-credit bar rather than enumerating requirements and waiving most; Internal Quality Checks row 34 was read only as interpretation. Frozen references/quality-checks.md:138-140 repeats this exact test. The frozen skill's whole-flow exception does not supersede qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:13: independent outcomes retain their own credit. Relevant deterministic workbook rows 29 and 33 and references/deterministic-checks.md:42-44 distinguish criterion schema/scoring from this semantic check.

Coverage: read every description in all five frozen judge.toml files, all five prompts, their injected tests/app_context.md, and the public brief/overview/behaviour/security/UI notes. A fresh read-only tomllib inventory measured Render 1 binary, Constraints 1 binary, Functional 58 binary, Polish 7 binary and Visual 6 Likert criteria, 73 descriptions in total; every file's ids were unique. This Pass concerns consistency of their stated full-credit targets, not completeness, independence under other QC rows, or implementation correctness.

All citations below are relative to .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/task/ unless stated otherwise. The two gates retain coherent bars: tests/gates/render/judge.toml:25 requires an actual authored marker in BOTH preview and console, and line 27's 'Grade only this ordinary successful run' excludes unrelated later features without waiving either output. tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:25 and :27 require a successful UI save, independent clean-context retrieval and reload of the same identity/fields; line 29's limitation to basic shared write/read does not waive those legs. tests/app_context.md:16 consistently makes the preparatory Auto-run-off step conditional on availability, while preserving the actual Run/output requirement.

Functional's tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:9 says 'Never ... inherit another row's verdict, or apply an all-legs score to a whole protocol'; :100 specifies that controls are facts rather than sibling pass flags. This resolves broad scenario prose against its explicitly named owners. I checked all 58 descriptions against their 23 protocols. Startup/example, filename dispatch/CSS/freshness, interaction/cancellation, sandbox/network, unsupported execution, deadline/rollback, four message/line/rollback families, console, Auto-run, editor, persistence/conflicts/titles, theme and shared-callback deadline all have a single conjunctive outcome or explicitly bounded shared-control requirement. The qualifiers narrow independent ownership rather than waive a criterion's own stated result. In particular: judge.toml:71 requires actual setter and fresh B execution while saying cancellation timing need not pass; prompt.md:182 expressly preserves those facts when cancellation fails. judge.toml:78 requires prior working script/handler markers, a retained visible enabled button, a successful ordinary click and no new old markers; its exclusion of colour/style belongs to the separate CSS outcome and does not permit absent controls. judge.toml:99 allows static/removed/disabled controls only AFTER an observed working handler and actual Stop. judge.toml:295 and :302 permit a failed debounce-reset sibling but still require positive automatic execution, the measured off/queue window and deliberate Run of the exact pending source, consistent with prompt.md:336-338. judge.toml:351 and :358 retain separate restart survival and post-restart writing targets, with the explicit fresh-record fallback in prompt.md:367. judge.toml:365 and :372 distinguish server refusal from actual dirty-editor recovery and preserve both trials; no prose allows a request replay alone to satisfy dirty-editor retention.

Potential ambiguity checked and not sustained: prompt.md:228 summarizes the S08 protocol as refusal 'without blocking legitimate text', but :220 explicitly assigns harmless-text failure to its own row and permits a separate ordinary baseline for unsupported-family probes. Together with :9 and :100, judge.toml:141 and :148 give a determinate result to an implementation that wrongly rejects harmless words but correctly refuses all five actual unsupported families: harmless_scope_words fails; unsupported_execution_refused can pass only on its own refusal, preservation and recovery evidence. Treating that protocol summary as an all-legs prerequisite would contradict the explicit scoring contract; it is not a second full-credit bar in either description. Similarly, the S10-S13 prose collects message, line and rollback evidence in one scenario, but their twelve separate descriptors and the global owner rule prohibit inheriting one result into another.

Polish: all seven descriptions agree with the P02 tour. tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:32, :41, :50 and :59 separately define names, keyboard reachability, visible focus on actually reached controls and a completed keyboard navigation route. The explicit rule at :50 that unreachable controls do not erase observed focus credit has one bounded domain, with a no-positive-focus failure rule; it is not a waiver of a preceding all-controls bar. Responsive layout permits stacking/tabs/scrolling while still requiring usable reachable panes; feedback and organisation judge their stated usability outcomes without importing execution/storage semantics.

Visual: all six descriptions have one anchor 5 plus descending 4-1 anchors. tests/scored/visual/judge.toml:25, :40, :55, :70, :85 and :100 each retain readability, contrast, separation, hierarchy, consistency or responsive composition as applicable. Native styling and harmless imperfections are explicitly compatible implementations of those bars, not permission to ignore them. The responsive exclusion of mobile operability/clipping at :99 is consistent with prompt.md:17-20, which limits the first five visual criteria to desktop and assigns mobile usability to Polish. The visual prompt's 'Full credit means clear, coherent presentation at the described level' (:41-42) agrees with the anchors.

Adversarial reading witnesses (reasoned, not executed app variants): (1) A conforming app with native menus, Escape-then-Tab editor escape and a static stopped preview remains eligible under Polish :41/:59 and Functional :99; no description adds a contradictory custom-control or live-after-Stop bar. (2) An app with working automatic execution but faulty debounce reset can still earn the two properly controlled off-state outcomes while failing debounce; neither their descriptors nor S17 require the failed sibling verdict. (3) A dead Auto-run feature cannot pass from silence because judge.toml:295/:302 and prompt.md:336 expressly require prior automatic authored execution. (4) A CSS implementation that removes/disables the copied button cannot pass inert copying despite producing no old logs because judge.toml:78 and prompt.md:137 explicitly reject that witness. (5) A static fake editor cannot pass the Render gate because its source text is expressly insufficient without both actual authored outputs. None supplies a plausible false pass or false fail caused by two competing full-credit bars.

Evidence limits: I inspected raw golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json metadata and independently hashed the frozen Functional descriptor and prompt bytes. They match raw functional_sha256 8e309112e55b495ff94bcc420483dc844b865bdf93cd3008522829914c2f3a2d and prompt_sha256 6405c6c52916b9480837a98b228a26e5fa0465241a3003d6da71b5f2bab907d1. Its scope is 'Continuous local reference browser proof; no LLM/provider/platform execution', and both pre/post criterion_verdicts_produced are false. I have not treated its pass flags or duration as configured-judge semantic validation, Oracle reward, target-model reward or judge timing. No paid, network, Docker or application mutation run was performed for this row. Runtime/model rows remain separate and unmeasured by this review.
